nodeData.note: Legumes and other covers that feed and protect the soil: cover crops, green manures and catch crops; the science (nitrogen, erosion, weeds, carbon); Kenya's best-bet legumes (mucuna, crotalaria, lablab, desmodium), seed rates, fitting them into maize, vegetable and plantation systems, when to cut or dig in, evidence, mistakes. Search: green manure, cover crop, velvet bean, sunn hemp, njahi, living mulch, catch crop.

children.note: A cover crop is grown to cover and protect the soil rather than to be harvested; a green manure is a cover crop that is cut or dug in while green to feed the soil. On small farms the two words overlap: the same legume can cover, feed the soil, feed the cow and feed the family.

children.note: Protects the soil surface from rain, sun and weeds between or under main crops; may be left as living cover or killed as mulch.

children.note: Grown for a few months, then slashed, mulched or ploughed in at or just after flowering, when biomass and nitrogen are highest.

children.note: A fast grass or cereal sown after harvest to catch leftover nitrogen before it leaches, releasing it when it decomposes.

links.label: 📄 Wikipedia: Cover crop

children.note: A low legume (desmodium, cowpea, lablab) growing between rows of maize or in an orchard all season.

children.note: A cover sown with a young plantation (coffee, tea, sugarcane, citrus) to hold the soil and smother weeds while the trees establish.

children.note: Legume roots house rhizobia that turn air nitrogen into plant nitrogen. A well-grown crotalaria or mucuna stand can hold 100–300 kg N/ha in its biomass — more than most crops need.

manas.q: How does a legume cover crop add nitrogen?

📄 Wikipedia: Cover crop

children.note: Infonet's sum: 8 t dry matter/ha × about 4 % N in leaves = roughly 320 kg N/ha if all is dug in. So part can be harvested as fodder and the rest still feeds the next maize.

manas.q: Roughly how much nitrogen does 8 t/ha of crotalaria biomass carry?

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: Leaves break the raindrop, stems slow runoff, roots bind soil. Kenyan trials showed soil loss dropping sharply once a legume cover was established; eroded soil is richer in C, N, P and K than what stays behind.

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes
📄 Wikipedia: Cover crop

children.note: Dense cover shades out weeds, saving weeding labour; mucuna, lablab and desmodium even suppress striga.

manas.q: Which green manure legumes suppress striga?

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: A global meta-analysis of cover-cropping found soil organic carbon about 15 % higher on average; mixtures beat single species and legumes beat grasses, with the gain in the top 30 cm.

links.label: 📄 Jian et al. 2020, Soil Biol Biochem: SOC meta-analysis (DOI)

children.note: Cover crops raised water infiltration about twofold and particulate organic carbon by about half in a 102-study synthesis; organic matter holds water in sandy soils.

links.label: 📄 Wikipedia: Cover crop

children.note: Deep roots pull up leached nutrients; mucuna after rock phosphate improved phosphorus availability in Nigeria.

links.label: 📄 Wikipedia: Cover crop

children.note: Cover acts as a push plant (desmodium against stemborers) and shelters predators and parasitoids.

children.note: 0–1,800 m, 4–12 months, about 7 t DM/ha in 6 months, 2.5–5.4 % N in leaves, excellent seed, smothers broad-leaved weeds and striga. Seeds contain L-dopa so they are not food without special processing; vines are fodder.

manas.q: Why are mucuna seeds not eaten without processing?

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: 0–1,900 m, matures in 3–4 months, about 8 t DM/ha, 3.6–4.7 % N, not toxic, leaves eaten as a vegetable, grows upright so it suits kale intercrops. Seed yield limited by pests.

manas.q: Which green manure is both a vegetable and an upright intercrop for kales?

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: 0–1,900 m, 3–12 months, about 8 t DM/ha, 3–5.8 % N, beans and leaves are food, good fodder, striga suppression like mucuna. Variety Rongai gives full ground cover in three months in dry Machakos.

manas.q: Which lablab variety was tested for conservation agriculture in Machakos?

children.note: 0–1,900 m, 6–12 months, about 5 t DM/ha, drought-hardy, excellent seed, but seeds are toxic (canavalin) and it is not fodder.

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: 0–1,900 m, perennial, 8–10 t DM/ha, 2.5–5 % N, good weed control, fodder; the push plant of push–pull.

children.note: 0–2,000 m, 12 months, 8–10 t DM/ha, 3.3–4 % N, good weed control, perennial fodder; goats gained weight on it in Katumani trials.

children.note: Cowpea, green gram, groundnut, pigeon pea, soybean and common bean fix less nitrogen for the soil (most goes to the grain) but still give cover and a harvest.

children.note: Plant the legume between maize rows at the same time or 1–2 weeks later to limit competition; after harvest it keeps growing through the short fallow and is dug in at land preparation.

manas.q: When is the legume planted in a maize intercrop, and why the delay?

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: Where maize is planted in April (e.g. Kitale), sow the legume in August between rows, strip lower maize leaves for light, harvest maize Nov–Dec and leave the legume as a short fallow until the next long rains.

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: Where the second season is unreliable (e.g. Kakamega), grow maize in the long rains, sow crotalaria or mucuna in September and incorporate in January–February.

links.label: 📄 Infonet-Biovision: Green manure / cover crop legumes

children.note: Lablab Rongai is left on the surface as mulch and maize is direct-planted into furrows cut through it; in semi-arid Machakos surface mulch gave better yields than digging in, because it saves moisture.

manas.q: In dry areas, is legume biomass better dug in or left on the surface?

children.note: Incorporating releases nitrogen faster (good in wet highlands); leaving as mulch saves water and protects soil (better in dry areas) but releases nitrogen more slowly.

children.topic: Combine with manure and small N doses
children.note: Kakamega trials: green manure plus farmyard manure plus a little nitrogen gave the highest maize yields; mucuna biomass alone raised maize yield 40–120 % across five sites.

manas.q: By how much did incorporating mucuna raise maize yields in the Kenyan network trials?

children.note: Because a good stand holds far more nitrogen than a crop needs, cut part for fodder or sell seed and still improve the soil.

children.note: 11,768 observations from 462 experiments: main crops after legumes yielded 20 % more on average, and 32 % more in low-yield, low-input environments such as much of Africa.

manas.q: How much more did main crops yield after legumes in the 2022 global synthesis?

children.note: Cover cropping increased soil organic carbon by 15.5 % on average; tropical soils gained less (about 7 %) than temperate ones, so expect slower change in Kenya.

links.label: 📄 Jian et al. 2020, Soil Biol Biochem: SOC meta-analysis (DOI)

children.note: A 2023 PNAS synthesis: intercrops give more total products per hectare and similar or better protein, with maize–legume pairs doing best at moderate nitrogen.

links.label: 📄 Li et al. 2023, PNAS: intercropping meta-analysis (DOI)

children.note: In semi-arid areas a cover crop can use water the next crop needs; termination timing matters, and long-term profit data are still thin.
